newsitem.title: UK: Brit Biotech says Zacutex result significant.
newsitem.headline: Brit Biotech says Zacutex result significant.

text.p: British Biotech Plc said on Monday that late-stage trials of its lead drug, acute pancreatitis treatment Zacutex, showed "statistically significant" results, including cutting death rates. In a statement the company also announced a series of senior marketing appointments as part of its strategy to build up an international sales team to market Zacutex and its most important drug, anti-cancer agent Marimastat.

The company is to present further details of British Phase III trials of Zacutex on 290 patients to the annual meeting of the American Gastroenterological Association later on Monday. The information confirms earlier data from the trials, which led the company to file its first application for regulatory approval in Europe. British Biotech said the trials showed fewer deaths in patients treated with Zacutex, and "this change was statistically significant in those patients treated within 48 hours of the onset of the disease." There was a also statistically significant reduction of organ failure three days after the start of treatment and a "significantly lower" incidence of pancreatic pseudocysts, a complication associated with acute pancreatitis.

It said no adverse effects were associated with the use of the drug. Acute pancreatitis is a serious inflammation of the pancreas which affects around 350,000 people in Europe and the U.S. each year. Sufferers require hospital treatment and around eight percent of patients die, usually because of multiple organ failure. The British Acute Pancreatitis Study Group said Zacutex "could be a useful new agent in the treatment of acute pancreatitis. There is a real need for an effective agent to treat these patients." British Biotech said it had set up sales subsidiaries in Britain, France, Germany, Italy, Scandinavia and Spain Last week the company said it would have a sales force of 45 in place for the launch of Zacutex in Europe, growing to 110 when the product was launched in the U.S.

It said its sales team could eventually rise to 500 depending on the success of Zacutex and Marimastat, which is scheduled for launch in 2000 if late-stage trials are successful. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
